mainTopic: The שעיר המשתלח (its remains, the meaning of עזאזל, and when the sender becomes טמא) and the burned פר and שעיר
overview: This amud joins a מחלוקת already in progress: may one benefit from the remains of the שעיר המשתלח? The permitting view learns from "במדבר" and the forbidding view learns from "גזירה". Each side then explains what it learns from the other side's word. רבא rules that the remains are permitted, because the תורה would not command "send" in a way that sets a trap. Several ברייתות then explain the name עזאזל: a hard, rough cliff in the wilderness, the hardest mountain, or atonement for the deeds of עוזא and עזאל. Another ברייתא contrasts משפטים, laws reason would demand, with חוקים such as the שעיר המשתלח, which ה׳ decreed and we may not dismiss. The גמרא then brings the views of רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, and רבי שמעון on when the sender's clothes become טמא. A new משנה describes the burned פר and שעיר: their אימורים are removed, the bodies are braided together and carried out, and the משנה gives a dispute about when the carriers' clothes become טמא. The גמרא corrects the משנה's wording, explains "קלען", and begins רבי's גזירה שוה for leaving the skin on, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Verse sources for permitting and forbidding the goat's limbs
steps.stepSummary: The permitting view learns from "במדבר". The forbidding view learns from "גזירה".
steps.simpleTranslation: [The one who permits the limbs learns it] from what is written: "in the wilderness." And the one who says they are forbidden learns it from what is written: "cut off" (גזירה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the verse source for each side of the argument about using the limbs of the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both words come from the same פסוק (ויקרא ט״ז:כ״ב). "במדבר" suggests the goat is like an ownerless wilderness, open to anyone, so it is מותר. "גזירה" suggests something decreed and cut off from use, so it is אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat sent away to עזאזל on יום כיפור

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The first line, "דכתיב במדבר", is the source for the view that PERMITS the limbs. That view was named on the previous amud.

phrases.english: as it is written: "in the wilderness."
phrases.notes: This is where the view that the limbs are permitted comes from.

phrases.english: And the one who says they are forbidden,
[learns it from] what is written: "cut off" (gezeira).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the מחלוקת earlier by supplying each side's verse
steps.raayaObject: Whether the limbs of the שעיר המשתלח are permitted or forbidden

steps.title: What does the forbidding view do with the word wilderness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the forbidding view learns from "מדבר".
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says they are forbidden, what does he do with this word "wilderness"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the forbidding side to explain the other side's word. This sets up an answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that every word in the תורה must teach something. If the forbidding view does not learn "permitted" from "מדבר", it must use the word for some other lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (holds a view)
What does he do with it?

phrases.english: And the one who says they are forbidden,
what does he do with this word "wilderness"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the forbidding view about the permitting view's verse
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the forbidding view learns from "מדבר"

steps.title: Wilderness includes the other places of the משכן and the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The forbidding view uses the three "wilderness" words to include נוב, גבעון, שילה, and the בית עולמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא: "into the wilderness," "into the wilderness," "in the wilderness" come to include נוב and גבעון, שילה, and the eternal Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the forbidding view needs "מדבר" for a different lesson, taken from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word wilderness appears three times about the goat. The extra mentions teach that the מצוה applied beyond the desert משכן. It also applied when the משכן stood in נוב, גבעון, and שילה, and in the בית המקדש. So the forbidding view has no extra word left to learn "permitted" from.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
Towns where the משכן later stood
The eternal house, meaning the בית המקדש in ירושלים

phrases.english: He needs it for that which was taught:
"Into the wilderness," "into the wilderness," "in the wilderness" —
to include Nov and Givon,
Shiloh, and the eternal Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "מדבר" is used to extend the מצוה to נוב, גבעון, שילה, and the בית עולמים

steps.title: What does the permitting view do with the word גזירה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks the permitting side what it learns from "גזירה".
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, what does he do with this word "גזירה"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same question around to the permitting side. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the permitting view must explain why the תורה wrote "גזירה", since that view does not learn a prohibition from it.

phrases.english: And the other one,
what does he do with this word "gezeira"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror question, now aimed at the permitting view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the permitting view learns from "גזירה"

steps.title: גזירה means a jagged place, or a goat that breaks apart
steps.stepSummary: The permitting view uses "גזירה" for a ברייתא. It means either a cut, jagged place or something that breaks apart as it falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught: "גזירה" means nothing other than cut. Another explanation: "גזירה" means nothing other than something that breaks apart and falls down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the permitting view needs "גזירה" for a ברייתא that explains the word in a physical sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first explanation says the goat must be sent to a place cut up with sharp rocks. The second says it refers to the goat breaking apart limb from limb as it falls. Either way, "גזירה" describes the place or the process, not a prohibition.

phrases.english: He needs it for that which was taught:
"Gezeira": gezeira means nothing other than cut.
phrases.notes: A place cut up by jagged rocks

phrases.english: Another explanation:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין גְּזֵירָה אֶלָּא דָּבָר הַמִּתְגַּזֵּר וְיוֹרֵד.
phrases.english: gezeira means nothing other than something that breaks apart and falls down.
phrases.notes: The goat is torn limb from limb as it falls

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "גזירה" describes a jagged place or the goat breaking apart, not a prohibition

steps.title: גזירה teaches that this is God's decree, not to be questioned
steps.stepSummary: A third explanation in the ברייתא: "גזירה" means God decreed this ritual, so one may not dismiss it as meaningless.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: "גזירה." Lest you say it is a meaningless act, the verse says "I am ה׳." I, ה׳, decreed it, and you have no right to question it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third meaning of "גזירה". It is a decree from ה׳, and we may not doubt it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sending a goat off a cliff can look pointless. The word "גזירה" is read as "decree" to block that thought. The ritual is a חוק from ה׳, and its authority does not depend on our understanding it.
steps.whatToRemember: Each side learns its view from one word and uses the other side's word for a different lesson. "מדבר" extends the מצוה to every Temple site. "גזירה" describes a jagged place, the goat breaking apart, or God's unquestionable decree.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the idea of a חוק. Some מצוות are kept as God's decree even when their reason is hidden, and we are not to dismiss them.

phrases.english: Another explanation: "gezeira":
lest you say it is a meaningless act,
the verse states: "I am ה׳":
I, ה׳, decreed it,
and you have no right to question them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״גְּזֵירָה״, שֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר מַעֲשֵׂה תֹהוּ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third explanation to the same ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "גזירה" signals a divine decree that may not be questioned
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The permitting view uses "גזירה" for these teachings, so it does not learn a prohibition from it

steps.title: רבא sides with the view that the goat's remains are permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the permitting view makes more sense, because the תורה would not command "send" in a way that leads people into a stumbling block.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It makes sense to follow the opinion that the goat's remains are permitted. The תורה did not say "send" (the goat away) in order to cause a stumbling block.
steps.whatsHappening: After hearing both sides' sources, רבא steps in and decides which view is more logical: the goat's remains are permitted for benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the goat is pushed off the cliff, nobody guards its body. If it were forbidden, a passerby could easily find it and use it without knowing, so the מצוה itself would create a trap. The תורה's word "שלח" (send away) suggests the job is finished once the goat is sent, with no lasting danger left behind.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical / it makes sense
Send (away), the Torah's command about the goat
A stumbling block / a trap that leads to sin

steps.whatToRemember: רבא concludes that the remains of the שעיר המשתלח are permitted, because the תורה would not build a trap into a מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general principle: the תורה's commands are not read in a way that sets people up to sin by accident.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is reasonable to follow the one who said they are permitted,
the Torah did not say "send" to cause a stumbling block.
phrases.notes: If it were forbidden, an unguarded carcass would easily lead people to sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר מוּתָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the dispute whose two sides were explained in steps 2 to 6 by choosing the permitting view on logical grounds.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The goat's remains are permitted, since the תורה's "send" was not meant to create a stumbling block.

steps.title: עזאזל means a hard, rough cliff in the wilderness
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads עזאזל as "strong and hard". It uses "במדבר" to rule out a settled area and "גזירה" to require a cliff.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "עזאזל" means the place should be strong and hard. I might have thought it could be in a settled area, so the verse says "in the wilderness." And how do we know it must be a cliff? The verse says "גזירה" (a cut-off place).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section: a ברייתא explaining what kind of place עזאזל must be. It works step by step through three words in the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word adds one detail. עזאזל, read as עז (strong) and קשה (hard), tells us the place is rough. "במדבר" removes the possibility of a settled area, and "גזירה" (a cut, jagged place, as in step 5) tells us it must be a cliff.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the goat is sent; here read as עַז (strong) + hard
"The verse teaches", a formula that introduces a proof from a פסוק

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Azazel" means that it should be strong and hard.
phrases.notes: Reads עזאזל as coming from עַז, strong.

phrases.english: I might think it can be in a settled area,
so the verse says: "in the wilderness."
And from where do we know it is at a cliff?
The verse says: "gezeira" (a cut-off place).
phrases.notes: Matches the first explanation of גזירה from step 5.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the dispute about the remains to explaining the place called עזאזל. It uses גזירה in the sense given in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The goat must be sent to a hard, rough cliff in the wilderness, not to a settled area.

steps.title: Another reading: עזאזל is the hardest of the mountains
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא reads עזאזל as "the hardest of mountains" and proves that "אל" can mean mighty or hard from a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: "עזאזל" means the hardest of the mountains. And so it says: "And the mighty ones (אילי) of the land he took."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא that also explains עזאזל, this time as the strongest, hardest mountain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word is split into עזז (strong) and אל, with אל meaning mighty or hard. The proof is the פסוק "אילי הארץ", which means "the mighty ones of the land" and shows that אל can carry the sense of strength.

keyTerms.meaning: The mighty ones of the land (יחזקאל יז:יג)
"And so it says", which introduces a supporting פסוק

phrases.english: It was taught in another (ברייתא):
"Azazel" means the hardest of the mountains,
and so it says:
"And the mighty ones of the land he took."
phrases.notes: Shows that אל can mean mighty or hard, so עזאזל reads as עזז + אל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel explanation of the same word, now resting on the ending אל and supported by a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עזאזל refers to the hardest mountain, since אל means mighty.

steps.title: עזאזל atones for the sin of עוזא and עזאל
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל reads עזאזל as a hint to עוזא and עזאל, and says the goat atones for what they did.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: "עזאזל" is so called because it atones for the actions of עוזא and עזאל.
steps.whatsHappening: A third explanation of the name עזאזל is given. This one is about what the goat accomplishes, not about the shape of the place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name sounds like עוזא and עזאל, angels or "sons of God" who according to tradition sinned with human women before the מבול and led the world into sin. This reading ties the name to the goat's purpose, which is atonement for that kind of corruption.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
Two fallen angelic beings linked to the sins before the מבול

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a third physical description of the cliff. It explains the name by what the goat atones for.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Azazel" because it atones
for the actions of Uzza and Azael.
phrases.notes: This is about בראשית ו:ב, the "sons of God" and the daughters of men.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different kind of explanation of the same name. Steps 8 and 9 were about the place; this one is about the goat's spiritual purpose.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name עזאזל points to atonement for the deeds of עוזא and עזאל.

steps.title: "My ordinances" are laws that logic alone would require
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא explains "את משפטי תעשו": משפטים are laws that would have deserved to be written even if the Torah had not written them. These are idol worship, forbidden relations, murder, theft, and cursing God.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "You shall do My ordinances." These are matters that, had they not been written, it would have been right for them to be written. They are: idol worship, forbidden relations, bloodshed, theft, and "blessing" (that is, cursing) God's Name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new ברייתא that sorts the Torah's laws into categories. This passage gives the first category, the משפטים, which human reason itself would demand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא defines משפטים as laws our own sense of right and wrong would arrive at. It lists five clear examples. This sets up a contrast with חוקים, laws whose reasons we do not understand, such as the שעיר המשתלח (compare step 6: one may not call it meaningless).

keyTerms.meaning: My ordinances, laws that make sense to human reason
Literally "blessing God", a polite way of saying cursing God

steps.confusionAlert: "ברכת השם" here does NOT mean blessing God. It is a polite substitute for cursing God's Name. The "(לא)" in parentheses is a textual note; the meaning is "had they not been written."
steps.whyThisMatters: This division prepares for the contrast with חוקים. That contrast explains why the שעיר המשתלח, a חוק, must be kept even though its reason is not obvious.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "You shall do My ordinances":
these are matters that, had they not been written,
it would be logical that they be written,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְגִלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת,
phrases.english: and these are they: idol worship, and forbidden relations,
and bloodshed, and theft, and "blessing" (cursing) the Name.
phrases.notes: ברכת השם is a polite way of saying cursing God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about kinds of מצוות. It connects back to step 6's point that the goat ritual is a divine decree, not to be dismissed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משפטים are laws that reason would demand: idol worship, forbidden relations, murder, theft, and cursing God.

steps.title: Statutes that the Satan challenges, and why we must not doubt them
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now explains "את חוקתי תשמרו". חוקים are מצוות that the Satan mocks, such as pork, שעטנז, חליצה, טהרת מצורע, and the שעיר המשתלח. The words "אני ה׳" teach that ה׳ decreed them, so we have no right to question them.
steps.simpleTranslation: "You shall keep My statutes" refers to things the Satan argues against. These are eating pork, wearing שעטנז, חליצה with a יבמה, the purification of a מצורע, and the goat that is sent away. In case you would say these are meaningless acts, the verse says "I am ה׳": I, ה׳, decreed them, and you have no right to second-guess them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the previous step continues. Having defined משפטים, it now defines the opposite group, חוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משפטים are laws that human logic would arrive at on its own. חוקים are laws with no clear reason, so outsiders, called here "the Satan", attack them as pointless. The words "אני ה׳" answer the attack. The authority behind these מצוות is ה׳ Himself, not our understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: Statutes: מצוות without an obvious reason
The Satan argues against them or mocks them
A garment mixing wool and linen

steps.whatToRemember: משפטים are laws logic would demand anyway. חוקים are decrees we keep because ה׳ commanded them, and the שעיר המשתלח is one of them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the שעיר המשתלח, the subject of this whole פרק, belongs among the classic חוקים. It is an act we perform without needing to understand it.

phrases.english: "You shall keep My statutes"
refers to matters that the Satan argues against,
and these are: eating pork,
and wearing a wool-and-linen mixture,
and the חליצה ceremony with a יבמה,
and the purification of a מצורע, and the goat that is sent away.
And in case you would say they are meaningless acts,
the verse teaches: "I am ה׳",
meaning, I, ה׳, decreed it,
and you have no permission to doubt them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 11 by defining חוקים as the counterpart to משפטים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוקים, including the שעיר המשתלח, are divine decrees that must be kept without questioning their reason.

steps.title: Only the sender himself becomes impure, not his escorts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's question about when the clothes become טמא. It opens with a ברייתא: the one who sends the goat becomes טמא, but the person who accompanies the sender does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה asked: when does he make his clothes טמא? The Rabbis taught: the one who sends the goat makes his clothes טמא. The one who escorts the sender does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words "אימתי מטמא בגדים" to open a new topic. It brings a ברייתא that first sets out who becomes טמא, which prepares for the next question of when.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before deciding the timing, the ברייתא limits the טומאה to one person, the actual sender. People who walk along with him, which the משנה described earlier, stay טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: "When does he make his clothes impure?" (quoting the משנה)
The one who sends the goat away
The one who escorts or sends off the sender

phrases.english: The משנה asked: "When does he make his clothes impure?"
The Rabbis taught in a ברייתא:
The one who sends the goat makes his clothes impure,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַשּׁוֹלֵחַ אֶת הַמְשַׁלֵּחַ מְטַמֵּא בְּגָדִים.
phrases.english: but the one who escorts the sender does not make his clothes impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the excursus on עזאזל and חוקים and returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the actual sender's clothes become טמא, not those of his escorts.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: impurity begins once he leaves the wall of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: Two words of the פסוק narrow down the timing. "המשלח" teaches that the טומאה does not start right at the עזרה wall. The extra "ו" in "והמשלח" teaches that it does not wait until the cliff. The middle point is the wall of ירושלים. This is רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he becomes טמא as soon as he leaves the wall of the עזרה, so the verse says "the one who sends". If it said only "the one who sends", you might think he becomes טמא only when he reaches the cliff, so the verse says "and the one who sends". How do these fit together? He becomes טמא once he leaves the wall of ירושלים. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now uses the פסוק to answer when the sender's clothes become טמא, and lands on a middle point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "המשלח" means a person who is actively sending. So simply stepping out of the עזרה is too early, because the real sending journey has not begun. The added "ו" expands the rule so it does not wait for the very end at the cliff. Squeezed between both limits, רבי יהודה sets the point at leaving the wall of ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: "One might think": introduces a possible mistake
The wall of the Temple courtyard
The wall of the city of ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: The same word "המשלח" is used twice in two different ways. Without the ו, it pushes the time later, past the עזרה. With the ו, it pulls the time earlier, before the cliff.

phrases.english: One might think: from when he goes out beyond the wall of the עזרה.
So the verse teaches: "the one who sends" (only once the sending is underway).
If it said only "the one who sends", one might think: not until he reaches the cliff.
So the verse teaches: "and the one who sends" (the extra ו includes an earlier point).

phrases.aramaic: הָא כֵּיצַד: מִשֶּׁיֵּצֵא חוּץ לְחוֹמַת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.english: How so? From when he goes out beyond the wall of ירושלים,
these are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: יכול משיצא חוץ לחומת עזרה תלמוד לומר המשלח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing who becomes טמא, the ברייתא now derives when.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the sender's clothes become טמא once he exits the wall of ירושלים.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: impurity begins when he reaches the cliff
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reads the words "עזאזל וכבס" side by side. The washing, and so the טומאה, connects to arriving at עזאזל, which is the cliff.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: the verse says "to עזאזל, and he shall wash". This means he does not become טמא until he has reached the cliff.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא disagrees with רבי יהודה and moves the moment of טומאה later, to the cliff itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי learns from the order of the words: "עזאזל" comes right before "וכבס". So the טומאה that requires washing only begins once he reaches עזאזל, the cliff.

keyTerms.meaning: "To עזאזל, and he shall wash": adjacent words in the פסוק

phrases.english: רבי יוסי says:
"to עזאזל, and he shall wash":
not until he has reached the cliff.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה and places the טומאה later, at the cliff.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, the clothes become טמא when he reaches the cliff.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: impurity begins only when he pushes the goat off
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reads the whole פסוק as describing the completed act of sending the goat to עזאזל. So the טומאה starts only when he throws it down headfirst.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: "And the one who sends the goat to עזאזל shall wash his clothes." He throws it down headfirst, and then he makes his clothes טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: A third תנא gives the latest point of all: the moment the goat is actually pushed off the cliff.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, "sending the goat to עזאזל" means finishing the job, not just arriving. Only after he throws the goat down does he count as "the one who sent", and only then do his clothes become טמא. The three views form a ladder: the wall of ירושלים, then reaching the cliff, then pushing the goat off.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall wash his clothes (a sign of טומאה)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three opinions on when the sender becomes טמא. רבי יהודה says when he leaves the wall of ירושלים. רבי יוסי says when he reaches the cliff. רבי שמעון says when he pushes the goat off.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון says:
"And the one who sends the goat to עזאזל
shall wash his clothes":
he throws it down headfirst, and only then makes his clothes impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי שמעון אומר והמשלח את השעיר לעזאזל יכבס בגדיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third, latest point in the dispute, after רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the clothes become טמא only once the goat is thrown off the cliff.

steps.title: The כהן גדול removes the altar parts from the burned bull and goat
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the כהן גדול tearing open the פר and שעיר הנשרפין, taking out their אימורים, and putting them in a bowl for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: He came to the bull and goat that are burned. He tore them open and took out their altar parts. He put them in a big bowl and burned them on the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. After the שעיר המשתלח is sent off, the כהן גדול turns to the פר and שעיר whose blood was brought inside, and takes out the fats meant for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two animals are not eaten; most of their body is burned outside. Only the אימורים, the fat parts, go on the מזבח. The משנה says he 'burned them,' and the גמרא will soon question that wording.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull and goat of יום כיפור whose bodies are burned outside
The fat parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל פַּר וְשָׂעִיר הַנִּשְׂרָפִין,
phrases.english: He came over to the bull and goat that are burned,
he tore them open and took out their altar portions,
phrases.notes: He tore them open; he did not cut them into neat pieces at this point.

phrases.english: he put them in a large bowl
and burned them on the altar.
phrases.notes: The גמרא will soon fix this wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל פַּר וְשָׂעִיר הַנִּשְׂרָפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה opens. It moves from the שעיר המשתלח to the burned פר and שעיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אימורים of the פר and שעיר הנשרפין are taken out and placed in a bowl for the מזבח.

steps.title: The bull and goat are braided together and carried out to be burned
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the animals are bound together and brought to the burning place.
steps.simpleTranslation: He wove them together like braids and took them out to the burning place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. The remaining bodies of the פר and שעיר are tied together and carried to the place where they are burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'קלען' is unusual. The גמרא will explain it with רבי יוחנן's statement that it means 'like a braid.' The burning place is outside ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: He wove them into braids, binding the pieces together

phrases.english: He interwove them into braids
and took them out to the burning place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה. After the אימורים are removed, the rest of the animals are taken out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bodies are bound together and carried to בית השריפה.

steps.title: When the carriers' clothes become טמא: dispute of תנא קמא and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: תנא קמא says the clothes become טמא once the animals leave the עזרה wall. רבי שמעון says it starts only once the fire has caught most of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when do they make clothes טמא? From when they go out past the wall of the עזרה. רבי שמעון says: from when the fire has caught most of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks at what moment the people handling the פר and שעיר become טמא, and two opinions are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the one who burns them must wash his clothes. תנא קמא starts the טומאה early, as soon as the animals leave the עזרה. רבי שמעון reads 'burning' strictly, so the טומאה starts only when most of the animal is burning. This matches how he started the שעיר המשתלח's טומאה only at the final act (step 16).

keyTerms.meaning: The wall of the Temple courtyard
From when the fire has caught most of them

steps.whyThisMatters: This repeats the same kind of timing question as the שעיר המשתלח. רבי שמעון again ties the טומאה to the finished act.

phrases.english: And from when do they make clothes impure?
From when they go out beyond the wall of the courtyard.
Rabbi Shimon says:
From when the fire has caught in most of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה moves from what is done to the animals to when they cause טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: the טומאה starts when they leave the עזרה wall. רבי שמעון: it starts when the fire catches most of them.

steps.title: Could the משנה really mean he burned the fats right away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the משנה's word 'והקטירן,' since the כהן גדול did not burn the אימורים at that moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'And he burned them'? Could you really think that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by challenging the wording of the משנה. This sets up a correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול still had other services to do first, so the burning of the אימורים happened later. Read literally, the משנה would mean he burned them right then, and that cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (a sign that a reading cannot be right)
And he burned them (on the מזבח)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
'And he burned them'? Would that enter your mind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins on the משנה by attacking the wording of step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The burning could not have happened at that moment, because other services came first.

steps.title: Correct the wording: he set them aside to burn later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה as 'in order to burn them' on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: in order to burn them on the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the משנה. He put the fats in the bowl so that they could be burned later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing 'and he burned them' to 'in order to burn them' solves the timing problem. The bowl holds the אימורים until their proper time.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (it should be read as)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the אימורים were burned right after they were removed. They were only set aside for later.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
in order to burn them on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא לְהַקְטִירָן עַל גַּבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the fats were burned immediately.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fats were placed in the bowl to be burned later.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן explains 'קלען': like a braid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the pieces were woven together like a braid.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He interwove them into braids': רבי יוחנן said, like a kind of braid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's word 'קלען,' and רבי יוחנן explains what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pieces were bound into one connected mass, the way strands are woven in a braid. This way they could be carried together.

phrases.english: 'He interwove them into braids.'
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Like a kind of braid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain the next phrase of the משנה (step 18).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'קלען' means binding the pieces together like a braid.

steps.title: They were cut up with the skin still on
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that unlike an עולה, these animals were not skinned before being cut up.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: he did not cut them up the way an עולה is cut up. Rather, the skin stayed on the flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds a detail about how the animals were cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is skinned first and then cut into pieces. The פר and שעיר הנשרפין were cut into pieces with the skin left on, and they were burned together with the skin.

keyTerms.meaning: Cutting an animal into its parts
A burnt offering, which is skinned before it is cut up

phrases.english: It was taught:
He would not cut them up
in the way the flesh of a burnt offering is cut,
but rather with the skin on top of the flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא לֹא הָיָה מְנַתְּחָן נִיתּוּחַ בְּשַׂר עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds how the animals were cut before being braided together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פר and שעיר הנשרפין are cut up with the skin left on, unlike an עולה.

steps.title: What is the source for leaving the skin on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the skin stays on.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these things learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's rule. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in step 23 needs a basis in the פסוקים. The גמרא is asking for it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the skin is left on the flesh.

steps.title: רבי begins a גזירה שוה: 'skin, flesh, and dung' appears in both places
steps.stepSummary: רבי points out that the same phrase 'עור ובשר ופרש' appears both here and by the other burned bulls. This is the opening of a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי says, 'skin and flesh and dung' is said here, and 'skin and flesh and dung' is said there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. רבי starts linking the יום כיפור animals to the other burned פרים through matching words. The rest of the proof continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Here' is ויקרא טז:כז, about the יום כיפור animals. 'There' is ויקרא ד:יא, about the פר כהן משיח. Because the same words appear in both places, the laws of one can be learned from the other. The lesson about leaving the skin on is still coming.

keyTerms.meaning: Skin, flesh, and dung: the matching words in both פסוקים
It says here, and it says there (the setup of a גזירה שוה)

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi says:
it is stated here 'skin and flesh and dung,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:כז, the יום כיפור bull and goat.

phrases.english: and it is stated there 'skin and flesh and dung,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ד:יא, the other burned bulls. The proof continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי אוֹמֵר נֶאֱמַר כָּאן עוֹר וּבָשָׂר וָפֶרֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה built on the words 'עור ובשר ופרש' (the proof is completed on the next amud).
